vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: frontend
Version: 1.0.2

The skill bundle provides read-only guidance and code examples for frontend design, explicitly stating in `SKILL.md` that it 'NEVER makes network requests, accesses user data, or stores any information' and `requires` no external `bins`. All other `.md` files contain only documentation and illustrative code snippets for frontend development, with no executable commands, network calls, or file system operations. There is no evidence of prompt injection, data exfiltration, malicious execution, or persistence mechanisms.

llm.summary: This frontend guidance skill is mostly coherent, but it includes under-disclosed commands that can execute mutable third-party npm code despite claiming read-only behavior.

dimensions.detail: The package says the skill never makes network requests and is read-only guidance, but the documented setup commands may access the network and modify a project when followed.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: stack.md instructs use of `npx shadcn@latest init` and `npx shadcn@latest add ...`, which can download and execute the current npm package version rather than a reviewed pinned version.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The activation language is broad but still centered on web UI work; I did not find prompt hijacking, hidden role changes, data collection, or unrelated task instructions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: I found no scripts, background workers, credential handling, persistent memory writes, services, scheduled tasks, or privilege escalation instructions in the artifact.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill's stated purpose is frontend UI guidance for React, Next.js, Tailwind, and related tooling, which matches the included design, mobile, typography, color, animation, and stack files.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this skill before installing if your agent may execute setup commands automatically. The design guidance is low risk, but use a pinned and reviewed shadcn version, run package setup only in projects you trust, and expect those commands to modify local files and potentially use the network.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: The broad frontend trigger is imprecise, but it is still aligned with the skill's stated UI-building purpose and does not by itself create a security concern.
[RP1] expected: shadcn setup is purpose-aligned for a frontend skill, but the use of `@latest` is an under-disclosed supply-chain risk because it can execute changing third-party code.
[T08] expected: The static finding is supported by stack.md: the commands are not automatic, but following them can run mutable npm CLI code with the user's normal project permissions.
